summary.summary: This is Cyngor Gwynedd's own 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, still marked 'Subject to Audit', going to the council's Governance and Audit Committee. The balance sheet is solid: long-term borrowing fell from £90.1m to £69.4m over the year, total reserves grew from £592.7m to £644.6m, and the unearmarked General Fund balance nearly doubled from £7.9m to £14.5m after a deliberate top-up. The Capital Financing Requirement rose to £188.5m (from £179.9m) even as external borrowing fell, meaning the council is increasingly relying on internal borrowing rather than new external debt. The narrative notes real budget pressure — a £6.6m in-year overspend concentrated in adult/children's care and waste — but there is no exceptional financial support, capitalisation direction, or section 114-type language anywhere in the document.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd has £16m of new capital money against £19.76m of requests, and built 118 homes against 247
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council's Cabinet has been told it has about £16m in additional money for capital spending (spending on things that last, such as buildings and flood defences) but requests from education and flood prevention projects come to £19.76m, a gap of £3.76m. The council's Capital Strategy says: "Given that there is currently £16M of additional resource available, it is not possible to fund everything and therefore, there will be a need to prioritise."

The £16m has built up since the council approved its 2024-2034 Asset Plan. It comes from capital grants, receipts, and £3.5m released by de-committing the Health and Care Hub project. The papers do not say which schemes will be funded or dropped.

A separate report to the meeting, the Annual Monitoring Report, covers housing. It records 118 homes completed in the Gwynedd Planning Authority area in 2025/26. That is 129 fewer than the annual average requirement of 247 (52.2% below) and 107 fewer than the forecast trajectory of 225. Since the local plan was adopted in 2017, 2,805 homes have been completed against a trajectory of 3,712, which is 24.4% below.

news_drafts.headline: Gwynedd took out no new loans in first quarter of 2026/27, leaving borrowing at £73.9m
news_drafts.lead:
Gwynedd Council took out no new loans in the first quarter of 2026/27, and its total borrowing stood at £73.9m, unchanged from 31 March. The figures are in the treasury management update (the report on how the council borrows and invests its spare cash) that went to its Governance and Audit Committee on 29 September.

The council says this is deliberate. It is using what is known as internal borrowing, meaning it pays for long-lasting spending from its own cash rather than taking a loan. This saves interest but uses up the cash cushion. The paper says the approach keeps borrowing below the council's underlying need.

The paper says the strategy "enabled the Council to reduce net borrowing costs (despite foregoing investment income) and reduce overall treasury risk". In other words, cash that is spent in place of a loan no longer earns interest as an investment, but the council judges the interest it saves on loans to be worth more. Its net investments stood at £11.4m.

findings.headline: 160MW Alaw Môn Solar Farm granted planning permission in August 2025; major renewable energy infrastructure investment approved
findings.detail: One commercial-scale renewable energy development was approved in the monitoring period: Alaw Môn Solar Farm (Enso Energy, 160MW). This represents significant capital investment in renewable energy infrastructure. Multiple other renewable projects remain in progress, including Morlais tidal arrays (240MW), Parc Solar Traffwll (35MW), and Porth Wen Solar Farm (49.99MW, now operational).
findings.matters: Major renewable energy project approval signals ongoing capital investment and economic activity in the area. Permitted renewable schemes total 3,421.60 GWh potential, supporting future business rates and employment from green energy sectors.
findings.figures: 160MW capacity approved; total permitted schemes potential 3,421.60 GWh
findings.quote: In this monitoring period one new renewable energy commercial scale development was granted planning permission, namely Alaw Môn Solar Farm (Enso Energy) (160MW) (permission given in August 2025).

findings.headline: Employment land take-up at 5.189 hectares against annual target of 6.9 hectares in 2025/26
findings.detail: Employment land permissions fall 1.7 hectares short of the annual target in the monitoring period. Cumulative take-up since plan adoption totals 22.099 hectares. The council acknowledges that 'the economic climate is significantly different to when the Plan was adopted, and it is considered that this has had a considerable impact on the take up of employment land.'
findings.matters: Employment land take-up below target indicates slower than forecast business investment and economic growth in the area, directly affecting future business rates income and employment prospects. Underperformance reflects weaker economic conditions than plan assumptions.
findings.figures: 5.189 hectares achieved vs 6.9 hectares annual target (-1.7 hectares); cumulative 22.099 hectares since 2017 adoption
findings.quote: In Gwynedd, 5.189ha of land has received permission for employment use on safeguarded employment sites during the eighth Annual Monitoring Report period (AMB8). Target: 6.9 ha employment land on safeguarded sites taken up per annum in Gwynedd

findings.headline: 91 affordable housing units completed (77% of 118 total completions); 80% of new permissions meeting threshold included affordable housing
findings.detail: Affordable housing delivery is performing strongly. In 2025/26, 91 of 118 completed units were affordable (77%). For new permissions, 145 of 182 units meeting the affordable housing contribution threshold were granted with affordable housing conditions or legal agreements (80% compliance). Since plan adoption, 639 of 1,159 units completed have been affordable (55.1%).
findings.matters: Strong affordable housing delivery indicates the council is effectively implementing housing policy objectives, maintaining workforce stability, and potentially supporting community sustainability. This positive performance amid overall housing shortfall suggests policy is working in the affordable segment.
findings.figures: 91 affordable units of 118 completions (77%); 145 of 182 units meeting threshold (80%); cumulative 639 of 1,159 since adoption (55.1%)
findings.quote: 91 affordable housing units completed in 2025/26 which is 77% of the total completions for this year.

findings.headline: Wylfa Newydd nuclear power station Development Consent Order withdrawn by Horizon Nuclear Power in January 2021
findings.detail: The proposed nuclear power station project, which had been subject to a Development Consent Order application, has been terminated. Horizon Nuclear Power withdrew the application due to lack of investor funding and absence of government funding policy support. No associated development has commenced and the infrastructure permissions (A5025 improvements granted in 2018) remain unexercised.
findings.matters: A major planned capital investment and economic driver has been eliminated, removing expected future jobs, investment, and economic growth. A lender would need to understand how the loss of this significant infrastructure project affects broader regional economic development plans and the council's future revenue prospects.
findings.figures: None quantified in document regarding scale of cancelled investment
findings.quote: On the 27th of January 2021 the Development Order Application was withdrawn by Horizon Nuclear Power. The application was withdrawn due to the lack of investors in the project and the lack of a new funding policy from the Government.

findings.headline: 118 homes completed in 2025/26 against annual requirement of 247 units, a shortfall of 52.2%
findings.detail: Gwynedd completed 118 housing units in the monitoring period, 129 units below the annual average requirement of 247 and 107 units below the forecast trajectory of 225. Cumulative completions since plan adoption in 2017 stand at 2,805 units against a trajectory target of 3,712 units (24.4% below). This represents structural under-delivery of housing throughout the plan period.
findings.matters: Housing delivery below target constrains local economic growth prospects, affects council tax and business rates base growth, and signals whether the council is meeting national housing supply targets. Persistent shortfall indicates either planning constraints or weaker than forecast economic demand.
findings.figures: 118 completed vs 247 required (-52.2%); vs 225 trajectory (-47.6%); cumulative 2,805 vs 3,712 targeted (-24.4%)
findings.quote: In this AMR period, it is noted that 118 units have been completed in the Gwynedd Planning Authority area. The Annual Average Requirement is 247 units for Gwynedd alone (therefore 129 fewer units or -52.2%)
